setup: Unrack the bar onto your upper back
Walk out and stand with feet hip-width
execution: Step straight back, land on the ball of the foot
Drop the back knee toward the floor
Push through the front foot to step back in
faults: Don't step back onto a tightrope line
Don't slam the back knee into the floor
Don't let the front knee cave in
Don't lean forward to start the rep

notes: Unrack and rerack in a rack with the safety arms set. The lunges happen outside the rack where nothing catches the bar, so keep loads well within control and the space behind you clear.
Balance is the limit before strength is. Learn the movement with dumbbells or no load before adding a bar.
If you lose balance, step the back foot down wide and stand up; don't fight to save the rep.
Log the bar and plates together (total). Reps are per leg.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at hip height, figure facing right. The near leg steps back so both legs are visible. Bar seen end-on on the upper back.

keyPositions.label: Standing
keyPositions.describe: Standing tall with feet hip-width, bar on the upper back, hands just outside the shoulders.

keyPositions.label: Bottom
keyPositions.describe: Near leg has stepped back about a stride; back knee just above the floor, on the ball of the back foot. Front shin fairly upright, front knee over the mid-foot. Torso upright or slightly forward.

keyPositions.label: Return
keyPositions.describe: Driving up through the front foot, back foot returning beside it. Ends in the standing position.

ikHints: Bar stays over the middle of the front foot
guideBrief.barPath: Mostly straight down and up; drifts slightly back with the step
emphasise: Back knee drops straight down toward the floor
Stance stays hip-width, not on one line
